evidence.title: Trans-activating mutations of the pseudokinase ERBB3.
passages: While harboring little kinase activity, pseudokinases can still promote signaling and carry out important noncatalytic functions such as serving as scaffolding or docking platforms, regulatory domains, or structural elements [ 4 , 5 ].

For example, based on the recent cryo-EM ectodomain structures of ERBB2-ERBB3 [ 34 ], K279 is located in domain II of ERBB3 just after the dimerization arm, at the beginning of module 5, a module in direct contact with the dimerization arm of ERBB2, thereby potentially affecting dimer formation and stability; it is known that modules 2–7 of domain II are sensitive to alterations as demonstrated by the oncogenic mutation S310F of ERBB2 that directly stabilizes the dimerization arm of ERBB3 [ 34 ].
Between the TM helices and kinase domains, the A676T variant may favor the asymmetric, active conformation of the kinase domain through increasing the stability of the JM region.

evidence.title: Biochemistry, Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor
passages: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), also known as erythroblastic leukemia viral oncogene homolog 1 (ErbB1) or human epidermal growth factor receptor 1 (HER1), is a member of the erythroblastic leukemia viral oncogene homolog (ErbB) family of receptor tyrosine kinases that regulates cellular proliferation, differentiation, survival, migration, and tissue repair.
The ErbB receptor family comprises 4 structurally related receptors—EGFR, HER2 (ErbB2), HER3 (ErbB3), and HER4 (ErbB4)—that undergo ligand-induced homodimerization or heterodimerization.

evidence.title: Expression of ErbB3, ErbB4, and neuregulin‐1 mRNA during tooth development
passages: Abstract The receptor tyrosine kinases ErbB3 and ErbB4, which bind to various variants of neuregulin (NRG), play fundamental roles in neural development and in organs, which form through epithelial‐mesenchymal interactions.
Here, we demonstrate that NRG‐1 and the receptors ErbB3 and ErbB4 are expressed locally during rodent tooth development.
